Joe Lombardo

Republican candidate for Governor, Nevada · Incumbent

Governor of Nevada

Joe Lombardo is the Republican governor of Nevada. He was elected in 2022 after serving as Clark County Sheriff. He is running for a second term in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Lombardo stands

Taxes
Has pledged no new taxes and says he has kept that pledge since his first campaign. Opposes resetting property tax values.
Right-to-work
Supports keeping Nevada's right-to-work law and opposes repealing it. Has said the system benefits the state's labor community.
K-12 education funding
Proposes a 12% increase in per-student funding over the biennium in his two-year budget plan. Has not committed to raising funding to the national average.
Third-grade reading retention
Supports holding back third graders who do not read at grade level. He brought the policy back in his 2023 education bill, AB400.
Voter ID
Supports requiring photo ID to vote. He backed the 2024 voter ID ballot question publicly and with money.
Abortion
Has said he would personally support a 15-week limit. Says abortion rights are written into state law and should be left to Nevada voters.
Data centers and utility rates
His campaign says the state already has strong protections against shifting data center costs to ratepayers, with guidance set through the Public Utilities Commission. It gave no yes-or-no answer on a new law.
Corporate home ownership
Vetoed a 2023 bill to cap corporate ownership of homes. His campaign gave no yes-or-no answer on new limits.
Theft threshold
Proposes lowering the felony theft threshold from $1,200 to $750, as he called for in his 2025 State of the State address.
Death penalty
Supports the death penalty and opposes repealing it. He said in 2021 that it deters crime and is a solution for egregious crimes.
